answer: DeepWalk (Perozzi, Al-Rfou, and Skiena, 2014) transfers the word2vec/skip-gram framework from natural language to graph-structured data by treating graph vertices as words and random walks over the graph as sentences. Specifically, it first generates many truncated, fixed-length random walks starting from each vertex, which play the role of word sequences or text corpora. It then feeds these walk sequences into the skip-gram model with hierarchical softmax, learning a low-dimensional embedding for each node such that nodes co-occurring within a window along a walk (i.e., nodes near each other in the graph) have similar representations. This exploits the observation that the frequency distribution of vertices visited by short random walks follows a power law similar to word frequencies in natural language, so language-modeling techniques designed for word-frequency-skewed corpora apply naturally. The result is an unsupervised, scalable method that learns node representations capturing structural neighborhood information, which can then be used for tasks such as node classification.
